descripcion: Brewery founded in 1850 in central Aizuwakamatsu, a yamahai pioneer in Fukushima. Its Kaeigura kura can be visited and it has its own online shop.
Brewery founded in 1711 that brews junmai only, with naturally grown rice and its own water, and grows part of that rice itself. Own online shop.
Brewery founded in 1790 in Kitakata, with its own museum (Kitakata Fudokan) open to visitors. Works rice from its own fields.
Kitakata brewery whose Aizu Homare label gave Aizu sake its name outside the region. Sells from its own shop and its official Rakuten store.

descripcion: Nihonmatsu brewery that makes ginjo only and by hand only, fermenting in wooden vats and steaming in a wagama pot.
Nihonmatsu brewery with some three hundred years of history and fourteen consecutive golds at the national new-sake competition.
Brewery founded in 1955 in Aizuwakamatsu. Took over the Sharaku label when Higashiyama Shuzo closed and sells only through appointed distributors.
Brewery founded in 1794 on Nanokamachi street in Aizuwakamatsu. Its Yuri line is brewed by a mother and daughter, unusual in the trade.
Aizubange brewery working Gohyakumangoku rice grown within fifteen kilometers. It has no own site and sells only through appointed distributors.
